name: Dermastamp
lead: A dermastamp is a handheld microneedling tool that presses a pad of short needles into the skin in a stamping motion, as opposed to the rolling action of a dermaroller. It is discussed on looksmax.org for use on skin, brows, under-eye lines and as a way to help topicals penetrate.[1][2][3][4]

Laboratory research on related oscillating microneedle devices has looked at improving delivery of drugs such as imiquimod through the skin in basal cell carcinoma.[5][6] No published trials of dermastamps for appearance outcomes were found in the sources reviewed.
infobox: Skin texture, brows, lines, topical delivery

paras: No studies found. Research on a related oscillating microneedle pen (Dermapen) as a delivery method for imiquimod in nodular basal cell carcinoma has been published, as has a doctoral thesis on the topic, but these concern cancer treatment rather than cosmetic stamps.[5][6]

Looksmax.org threads include a user asking how often to stamp brows alongside minoxidil,[1] threads comparing a dermaroller with a dermastamp,[3] a thread asking whether a stamp can replicate a "microinfusion" treatment,[7] and a post that claims a stamping method removes laugh lines and eye lines.[4]

lore.intro: Looksmax.org posters discuss dermastamps for brows, skin and lines, mostly as an inexpensive alternative to clinic microneedling.[1][3][4]

claims.claim: A dermastamp can reduce laugh lines and eye lines
claims.believers: A poster presents a personal stamping method that they say removes expression lines.[4]
claims.experts: No published studies of dermastamps for expression lines were found; microneedling in general has been studied for scars and acne, with research ongoing.[8]

claims.claim: Stamping the brows alongside minoxidil can support brow growth
claims.believers: A user asks how often to stamp brows with nightly minoxidil, implying that the combination is common practice.[1]
claims.experts: Wikipedia notes that some studies found microneedling plus minoxidil outperformed minoxidil alone for hair loss on the scalp; brow-specific studies were not found.[8]

claims.claim: A stamp can replace clinic microinfusion treatments
claims.believers: Users ask whether a stamp can be used in the manner of a clinic microinfusion treatment.[7]
claims.experts: No studies were found comparing the two; infection concerns are noted for non-clinical microneedling.[8]

card.summary: A handheld needle-stamp used for DIY microneedling of skin and brows; no cosmetic trials found for the stamp itself.

quick.overview:
A dermastamp is a small stamp-like microneedling tool used at home. Forum users apply it to brows, skin and fine lines.

No trials of the stamp itself for appearance were found.
quick.mechanism: It presses short needles into the skin to create tiny punctures, which microneedling proponents say triggers repair and improves topical absorption.
quick.risks: Infection is a recognised concern with non-sterile or untrained microneedling, per Wikipedia. Device quality and hygiene vary.
